steps.title: Import React and React Router DOM
steps.instruction: Import React from 'react' and BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, and Link from 'react-router-dom'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the routing components from their respective packages.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and React Router DOM components here

// Your component will go below
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary imports for React and React Router DOM are added to the file.
successCriteria: The code includes an import statement for React from 'react' and imports BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, and Link from 'react-router-dom'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and the essential React Router DOM components. This sets up the foundation for implementing routing in your application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some of the required items, but not all. Make sure to import React from 'react' and BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, and Link from 'react-router-dom'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import React from 'react' and BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, and Link from 'react-router-dom' to proceed with routing.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty fragment (<></>) for now. This will be the main entry point for your application.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Make sure to export the component so it can be used elsewhere.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a functional App component that returns an empty fragment and is exported as the default export.
successCriteria: Component named App is created
Component returns an empty fragment (<></>)
Component is exported as default
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main App component. This will serve as the foundation for adding routing functionality in the next steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there are a few things to check. Make sure you've created a component named App, it returns an empty fragment, and it's exported as default.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't seem to be created correctly. Remember to create a functional component named App that returns an empty fragment (<></>) and export it as default.

steps.title: Create a Home component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Home that returns a heading element saying 'Home Page'.
steps.hint: Define a new component function called Home that returns JSX with an <h1> element containing the text 'Home Page'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Home component is defined and ready to be used in routing.
successCriteria: The Home component should be a function that returns an <h1> element with the text 'Home Page'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the Home component. This component will serve as the main landing page for your application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your Home component returns an <h1> element with exactly the text 'Home Page'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Home component wasn't created correctly. Remember to define a function named Home that returns JSX containing an <h1> with 'Home Page'.

steps.title: Create an About component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named About that returns a heading element saying 'About Page'.
steps.hint: Define a new component function or arrow function called About that returns JSX with an <h2> or similar heading containing the text 'About Page'.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new About component is defined and ready to be used in routing.
successCriteria: The code defines a component named About that returns a heading element with the text 'About Page'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the About component. This gives us a second page to route to in our application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your component is named exactly 'About' and returns a heading with the text 'About Page'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The About component wasn't created correctly. Remember to define a function or arrow function called About that returns JSX containing a heading with 'About Page'.

steps.title: Wrap App with BrowserRouter
steps.instruction: In your App component, wrap the existing content with the BrowserRouter component you imported earlier.
steps.hint: Use the BrowserRouter component as a wrapper around your Routes and Route components.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now returns content wrapped in BrowserRouter, enabling routing functionality throughout the app.
successCriteria: The App component's return statement should have BrowserRouter as the outermost element, wrapping the existing div and its contents.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wrapped your app with BrowserRouter. This provides the routing context needed for React Router to work.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure BrowserRouter wraps all the content in your App component's return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The BrowserRouter wrapper is missing or incorrectly placed. Remember to wrap your entire App content with <BrowserRouter> tags.

steps.title: Add Routes container
steps.instruction: Wrap the existing Routes component with a BrowserRouter component in the App component's return statement.
steps.hint: BrowserRouter should be the outermost wrapper that contains all your routing components.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now returns a BrowserRouter wrapping the Routes component, establishing the routing context for the application.
successCriteria: BrowserRouter component wraps the Routes component in the App's return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wrapped your Routes with BrowserRouter, which provides the routing context needed for React Router to work properly.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure BrowserRouter directly wraps the Routes component (remove any extra div wrapper if present).
steps.feedbackWrong: The BrowserRouter wrapper is missing or incorrectly placed. Remember to wrap the Routes component with <BrowserRouter>.</BrowserRouter> in the App's return statement.

steps.title: Define Home route
steps.instruction: Inside the Routes component, add a Route component with path='/' and element={<Home />}.
steps.hint: The Route component should be a child of Routes. Use the Home component you created earlier as the element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of a Route definition
<Routes>
  <Route path="/" element={<Home />} />
</Routes>
steps.expectedOutcome: The Home component will be accessible at the root URL (/) of your application.
successCriteria: The Routes component should contain a Route with path='/' and element={<Home />}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the route for the Home component. Now the Home page will render when users visit the root URL.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the Route component has both the correct path ('/') and the correct element (<Home />).
steps.feedbackWrong: The route definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to add a Route component inside Routes with path='/' and element={<Home />}.

steps.title: Define About route
steps.instruction: Inside the Routes container, add a second Route component with path='/about' that renders the About component.
steps.hint: Add another <Route> element after the existing Home route. Use path='/about' and element={<About />}.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding a route inside Routes
<Routes>
  <Route path="/home" element={<Home />} />
  <Route path="/about" element={<About />} />
</Routes>
steps.expectedOutcome: The Routes container now has two routes: one for the Home component at '/' and one for the About component at '/about'.
successCriteria: Add a Route component inside the existing Routes with path='/about' and element={<About />}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the About route. Now your app has two separate pages accessible at different URLs.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a Route component with both path='/about' and element={<About />} inside the Routes container.
steps.feedbackWrong: The About route isn't properly defined. Check that you've added a Route component with path='/about' and element={<About />} inside the Routes.

steps.title: Add navigation links
steps.instruction: Add a navigation section with Link components for '/' and '/about' paths inside the App component, before the Routes container.
steps.hint: Import Link from 'react-router-dom' and add a <nav> element with two <Link> components inside.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding navigation links
<nav>
  <Link to="/">Home</Link>
  <Link to="/about">About</Link>
</nav>
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will include a navigation bar with clickable links that navigate between the Home and About pages without full page reloads.
successCriteria: Import Link from 'react-router-dom'
Add a <nav> element inside the App component's return
Include two <Link> components with to="/" and to="/about"
Place the navigation before the <Routes> container
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added navigation links using the Link component. This allows users to navigate between pages without full page reloads.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've imported Link, added a <nav> element, and included both Link components with the correct 'to' paths.
steps.feedbackWrong: The navigation links aren't properly set up. Check that you've imported Link, added a <nav> element with two Link components inside, and placed it before the Routes container.

steps.title: Add active link styling
steps.instruction: Import NavLink from 'react-router-dom' to enable active link styling.
steps.hint: Add an import statement for NavLink from the same package you imported BrowserRouter, Routes, and Route from.
steps.expectedOutcome: NavLink is imported and ready to be used in the next step.
successCriteria: The import statement for NavLink from 'react-router-dom' is added correctly.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported NavLink. This component will allow you to add visual styling to indicate which link corresponds to the current page.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your import syntax. Make sure you're importing NavLink from 'react-router-dom' using the correct import statement format.
steps.feedbackWrong: NavLink hasn't been imported yet. You need to add an import statement for NavLink from 'react-router-dom' to proceed.

steps.title: Add a 404 route
steps.instruction: Add a Route component with path='*' that renders a '404 Not Found' message inside your existing Routes container.
steps.hint: Add a new <Route> element as a sibling to your existing routes. Use path='*' as a catch-all and provide an element prop with JSX containing a '404 Not Found' message.
steps.analogousExample: // Example of a catch-all route Page not found} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The app will now show a '404 Not Found' message when users navigate to any undefined route.
successCriteria: Add a Route component with path='*'
Include an element prop with JSX containing a '404 Not Found' message
Place it inside the existing Routes container
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a catch-all route that will display a 404 message for any undefined paths.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your Route has path='*' and renders a '404 Not Found' message.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding a Route component with path='*' that renders a '404 Not Found' message inside the Routes container.

steps.title: Test the routing
steps.instruction: Run your application and verify that you can navigate between the Home and About pages using the navigation links.
steps.hint: Start your development server (e.g., with npm start or yarn start). Click the 'Home' and 'About' links to see the content change. The active link should be highlighted.
steps.expectedOutcome: The application runs successfully, and clicking the navigation links switches between the Home and About pages with proper active link styling.
successCriteria: Application runs without errors
Navigation links work to switch pages
Active link is visually distinct
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Your routing setup is complete and functional. You've successfully implemented React Router basics with navigation and active styling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure all navigation links are working and the active link styling is applied correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that your development server is running and all route definitions are correct. Verify the navigation links are properly implemented.
